correctness.rationale: Normalize A to contain zero. The convolution identity at a∈A and nonnegativity force h(t)=0 on (A-A)\{0}. For every remaining x∉A the unknown values on allowed shifts solve integer incidence M_A h=ones. The standalone exact checker constructs each of the five group tables and iterates every one of the 2^15 normalized nonempty subsets; for every case, either allowed shifts fail coverage, an explicit compatible complement exists, or integer elimination finds rank_Q[M|1]>rank_Q M. Rational inconsistency excludes all real, hence nonnegative, solutions. Direct converse takes h=1_B for a tiling complement containing zero. I independently read and reran the complete deterministic Python checker, which terminated successfully with 163840 subsets and exact tile counts 1,15,95,139,1;1,15,183,371,1;1,15,311,387,1;1,15,359,787,1;1,15,455,1395,1. Exhaustiveness depends on transparent loop and exact group construction, not a sampled finite experiment.
residual_risks: The theorem is limited to five abelian groups of exactly 16 elements; neither order-32 nor nonabelian groups are covered.
The finite proof relies on algorithmic exhaustiveness of the supplied exact-integer checker; no formal Lean certificate is claimed.

originality.rationale: The primary Kiss--Matolcsi--Matolcsi--Somlai theorem defines normalized positive-definite weak tiling and proves low-dimensional elementary p-group results, not the five order-16 types without Fourier positivity. An earlier complete F2^4 census establishes one of the five cases exactly (counts 1,15,455,1395,1) and is acknowledged as known. Spectral/Fuglede censuses for Z4² and Z4×Z2² concern spectral sets rather than arbitrary nonnegative normalized weak complements. The other four group types and all-order-16 classification survive direct implication checks.

The finite proof relies on algorithmic exhaustiveness of the supplied exact-integer checker; no formal Lean certificate is claimed.
